claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi component state migrations are a new feature.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A component state migrations discussion exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering the callback contract.
The pulumi/examples repo has a directory aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration containing v1, v2, v3 programs and migration code.
The legacy component is `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc`, and the v1 example creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and association, and an internet gateway.
Replacing a VPC forces replacement of a security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId docs).
The modern AWSX component is `awsx.ec2.Vpc`.
The v3 example declares resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, while modern AWSX removes those wrappers; the subnet's Pulumi name changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1`.
Pulumi state records each resource with a URN, and managed resources also have a provider ID.
Aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
Migrations are registered through the `stateMigrations` resource option together with an alias for the legacy component type.

A state migration callback receives the saved state of the old component followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (complete replacement records) and `successors` (map from each disappearing old URN to its replacement URN).
Pulumi uses successors mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid.
The `rename` helper preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields while changing URN, type, and parent.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration, and after both have run callbacks return no result.
After a migration, Pulumi compares the new program with migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Running `pulumi preview` evaluates the migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.
When users upgrade a component that registers a migration, Pulumi runs the migration as part of the normal preview and update without users writing the migration or editing state.
State migration callbacks (the stateMigrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
State migration callbacks must be idempotent and must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
State migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration callback is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi state migration option reference page documents the callback API at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api.

State entries passed to component state migration callbacks use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs, as documented in the Pulumi developer docs deployment schema.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing migration results (under update plans or targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
